findings.title: Signs expose trajectories through present surfaces
findings.claim: Within this pericope, the comparison of flourishing matter with its brittle, scattered after-state makes the focus's signs and good news function as visible disclosures of trajectories, so present surfaces can expose what is coming and what endures.
findings.mechanism: The context carriers at 18:45:3, 18:45:15, and 18:45:16 show a comparison moving from living appearance to brittle fragments and dispersal, while 18:46:6 names what remains; those triggers meet the focus carriers at 18:56:5 and 18:56:15, making good-news and sign language read as early evidence of a course rather than bare future information.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive why the focus places good news, warning, and signs together: the surrounding comparison teaches signs to disclose a trajectory already beginning in the present.
findings.containment: This is a local pericope reading, not a claim that the comparison exhausts the messenger office. The live alternative supplied by the HFT is that 18:45 teaches transience without specifying the messenger function. The ordinary reading remains recoverable, and the contextual activations stay attributed because target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: Truth meets an inspectable record
findings.claim: The focus's attempt to dislodge truth is recast by the surrounding judgment sequence as a temporary management of appearance: what is covered can be exposed, displayed, enumerated, and made present as an inspectable record.
findings.mechanism: The context carriers at 18:47:6, 18:48:1, 18:49:2, 18:49:12, 18:49:19, and 18:49:23 move from exposure to public presentation, exhaustive writing, and present deeds; they contact the focus carriers at 18:56:9 and 18:56:13, so making truth slip meets a record that can be inspected rather than erased.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the focus's falsehood as an attempt to manage visibility inside a passage that later makes reality publicly present and countable.
findings.containment: This does not claim that the judgment scenes are only epistemic or that present argument has no effect. The HFT alternative is accountability without a comment on argumentative visibility. The focus's ordinary contrast between falsehood and truth remains intact.

findings.title: Mockery is a chosen role assignment
findings.claim: The taking construction in the pericope frames mockery as a chosen assignment of signs and warnings to a substitute role, analogous to taking allies or refusing supports, rather than only as an emotional reaction.
findings.mechanism: The context carriers at 18:50:16, 18:50:18, 18:50:26, 18:51:11, and 18:51:13 repeat adoption, alliance, substitution, and support; they contact the focus carriers at 18:56:14, 18:56:15, and 18:56:18, so taking signs and warnings as mockery becomes a selected functional use.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the verb's double-object force: the signs and warnings are not merely met by a feeling, but are placed into a role that serves the deniers' stance.
findings.containment: This does not turn every taking construction into mockery or assign intention beyond the focus. The repeated-role pattern remains an attributed contextual inference, while mockery keeps its ordinary sense and the live alternative that repetition marks selection without full allegiance force.

findings.title: Varied explanation becomes counter-material
findings.claim: The many-form examples immediately before the focus give disputation a way to recycle explanation itself, turning each new presentation into material for a false counter-case.
findings.mechanism: The context carriers at 18:54:2, 18:54:9, 18:54:12, and 18:54:14 place varied examples beside abundant contentiousness; they contact the focus carriers at 18:56:7, 18:56:10, and 18:56:11, where disputation uses falsehood to make truth slip, so variation becomes reusable counter-material rather than accumulated clarity.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the focus's argument as a reuse of explanatory abundance: more forms can become more surfaces for contest when the disputant's aim is refutation.
findings.containment: This does not claim that every varied example causes dispute. The live alternative is simple contrast between plentiful examples and human disputation, with no causal reuse implied. The ordinary sequence of disputing with falsehood to dislodge truth remains primary.

findings.title: Warning fills a merciful interval before appointment
findings.claim: The focus's warning-and-good-news mission occupies a merciful interval before a fixed consequence: delay gives a response window while the appointed endpoint remains.
findings.mechanism: The context carriers at 18:55:2, 18:55:19, 18:58:4, 18:58:6, 18:58:9, 18:58:14, 18:59:3, and 18:59:7 bracket the focus's send-and-warn carriers at 18:56:2, 18:56:3, 18:56:6, and 18:56:17; dispatch and warning therefore fill the interval between blocked response and a fixed appointment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive warning as an actionable form of mercy: respite is time in which a response remains possible, while the stated appointment still gives the interval an edge.
findings.containment: This does not make mercy identical with messenger warning or cancel the appointed consequence. The live alternative is that mercy alone explains postponed punishment without defining the entire messenger function. Warning, delay, and appointment remain distinct elements.

findings.title: Mockery recodes attention into closure
findings.claim: The focus's mockery can be heard as an attentional recoding that helps turn renewed signs into neglect, covering, uncomprehending hearts, and unreceiving ears.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers at 18:56:9 and 18:56:18 meet the context carriers at 18:57:4, 18:57:5, 18:57:7, 18:57:9, 18:57:17, 18:57:19, 18:57:21, and 18:57:22, where reminder is followed by turning away, forgetting, cover, and blocked comprehension and hearing; this makes mockery a recoding step in closure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see mockery as part of a process of attention: once a sign is classified as unserious, renewed reminders can be left unheard and unprocessed.
findings.containment: This does not claim that mockery alone causes the closure or that the next ayah is reducible to psychology. The live alternative is judicial enclosure after rejection rather than mockery participating in its formation. The primary rejection and mockery remain fully recoverable.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic anchors and HFT coordinates support the stated pericope contact, but the packet says target morphology is not supplied and the reader identity is legacy_unbound. The branch contacts therefore remain attributed contextual evidence.
